keyFindings.description: leaseHandBackBridge = lingerUntaken + leaseStandbyPoll = 1.5 s, but the stopping pod's linger ends 'not taken' about 1.0 s after its release (linger, receive.go). A pod that first takes the released record 1.0-1.5 s after it (a pod starting, a standby whose poll failed) counts as handed back and holds 3 s while a lost node's binding (stale_binding) has had the deliver subject alone since the linger ended; messages due from it at the 6 s ack wait arrive after newer ones. The lingerMax 'timeout' exit has the same gap. TestLeaseTakesAReleasedRecordPastTheLingerAsNoHandBack waits the whole window plus 100 ms, so the gap is untested.

letGo writes a release whenever held is true, including during a lapse (held stays true; only Holding() turns false). A term whose hold ended (unsettled and ack_wait_owed false) that lapses drops what it took without an ack (handle, endLost), and a SIGTERM before renew resumes releases the record clean: the next pod does not settle and delivers new messages before the dropped ones return at the ack wait. Before the release the record would have expired and the take-over settled 7 s.
